title: FOR A DECEASED MUSLIM
meaning: O Allah, forgive him and have mercy on him.
note: For a woman: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهَا وَارْحَمْهَا — Allāhumma-ghfir lahā warḥamhā.
source: Authentic funeral supplications include asking Allah to forgive and have mercy on the deceased.

title: WHEN CALAMITY STRIKES
arabic:
إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ
اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي، وَأَخْلِفْ لِي خَيْرًا مِنْهَا
translit: Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn. Allāhumma-jurnī fī muṣībatī, wa akhlif lī khayran minhā.
meaning: We belong to Allah and to Him we return. O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with something better.
source: Qur'an 2:156; Sahih Muslim 918.

title: WHEN DEATH IS NEAR: KEEP SALAH
bullets: If an obligatory prayer time enters and you remain conscious and legally responsible, pray according to your ability.
Stand if able; otherwise sit; otherwise lie down and use head movements as Hanafi fiqh permits.
Do not abandon the prayer merely because you are very ill.
If you lose the ability to make even the required head indication, detailed Hanafi rules apply; family should ask a qualified scholar.
source: Hanafi sick-person prayer fiqh.

title: DUʿA WHEN DEATH IS NEAR
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَارْحَمْنِي، وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالرَّفِيقِ الْأَعْلَى
translit: Allāhumma-ghfir lī warḥamnī, wa alḥiqnī bi-r-Rafīqi l-Aʿlā.
meaning: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and join me with the Highest Companion.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari 5674 and related reports from ʿAʾishah.

title: TALQIN FOR THE DYING
meaning: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.
bullets: Gently prompt a dying Muslim to say this testimony.
Do not badger or frighten the person; the purpose is gentle remembrance.
If the person says it and does not speak afterward, there is no need to keep repeating the prompt.
source: Sahih Muslim 916; Sunan an-Nasa'i 1827.

title: AROUND A DYING MUSLIM
bullets: Speak good words and make duʿā; angels say Āmīn to what is said around the dying or newly deceased.
Encourage hope in Allah’s mercy and a good opinion of Allah.
Avoid arguments, panic, or statements of despair.
After death, proceed with the Islamic funeral arrangements without unnecessary delay and contact knowledgeable local Muslims/imam.
source: Sahih Muslim 919; general funeral Sunnah.

title: DUʿA AL-QUNUT • PART 2
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ، وَلَكَ نُصَلِّي وَنَسْجُدُ، وَإِلَيْكَ نَسْعَى وَنَحْفِدُ، نَرْجُو رَحْمَتَكَ، وَنَخْشَى عَذَابَكَ، إِنَّ عَذَابَكَ بِالْكُفَّارِ مُلْحِقٌ
translit: Allāhumma iyyāka naʿbudu, wa laka nuṣallī wa nasjud, wa ilayka nasʿā wa naḥfid, narjū raḥmataka wa nakhshā ʿadhābak, inna ʿadhābaka bi-l-kuffāri mulḥiq.
meaning: O Allah, You alone we worship; for You we pray and prostrate; toward You we strive and hasten. We hope for Your mercy and fear Your punishment. Surely Your punishment overtakes the disbelievers.
note: Hanafi texts transmit accepted variants. Parts 1–2 together give one standard transmitted Hanafi form.
source: Classical Hanafi Witr/Qunut texts.

title: AYAT AL-KURSI • PART 2
arabic: وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ، وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ، وَلَا يَؤُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا، وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
translit: Wa lā yuḥīṭūna bi-shayʾin min ʿilmihī illā bimā shāʾ. Wasiʿa kursiyyuhu s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ. Wa lā yaʾūduhu ḥifẓuhumā, wa Huwa l-ʿAliyyu l-ʿAẓīm.
meaning: They grasp nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and earth; preserving them does not tire Him. He is the Most High, the Magnificent.
source: Qur'an 2:255; Sahih al-Bukhari 2311 on protection before sleep.

title: CHRONIC EXCUSE (MAʿDHUR)
bullets: Frequent gas alone does not automatically make someone legally excused.
The status begins only when an entire prayer time passes without a long enough break to make a minimal valid wudu and pray a quick fard prayer.
Once established, make wudu after the prayer time begins. That wudu remains usable during that prayer time despite the ongoing excuse.
It ends at the end of the prayer time, or earlier if wudu is broken by a different invalidator.
Because the qualification rules are technical, confirm your personal case with your imam.
source: Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance: chronic excuses and ablution.

title: MISSED FARD PRAYERS (QADA)
bullets: A missed fard prayer must be made up.
Pray the same number of fard rakʿahs the missed prayer required, subject to traveler/resident rules at the time it became due.
If fewer than six prayers are owed, Hanafi rules can require keeping order between missed and current prayers.
Once six or more are owed, strict ordering is no longer required.
Do not perform qada during the three completely prohibited windows: sunrise, zawal, and the actual sunset period.
source: Hanafi fiqh; Maraqi al-Falah; SeekersGuidance on qada order and prohibited times.

title: MISSED WITR
bullets: Witr is wajib in the Hanafi school.
If it is missed, make it up.
The hadith instructs one who slept through Witr or forgot it to pray it when remembered.
If you already prayed Witr and later wake for Tahajjud, pray your additional nafl but do not repeat Witr.
source: Hanafi fiqh; Abu Dawud/Tirmidhi reports on missed Witr; SeekersGuidance.

title: NO FIXED MAXIMUM OF NAFL
bullets: Beyond the fard and wajib prayers, there is no single daily maximum number of voluntary rakʿahs.
You may pray additional nafl in permitted times according to your ability.
Keep the confirmed Sunnahs and Witr as priorities rather than chasing a number.
Respect the restricted and prohibited prayer times.
source: General Hanafi fiqh of voluntary prayer.

title: SALAT AL-TASBIH: DISTRIBUTION
arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
translit: Subḥāna llāh, wa-l-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illā llāh, wa-llāhu akbar.
bullets: After the opening praise, before Qur'an recitation.
After Qur'an recitation while still standing.
In ruku after the normal ruku tasbih.
After rising from ruku.
In the first sujud after its normal tasbih.
While sitting between the two sujuds.
In the second sujud after its normal tasbih.
TOTAL
75 per rakʿah × 4 rakʿahs = 300.
source: Method attributed to Ibn al-Mubarak and transmitted in the Salat al-Tasbih reports.

title: BEFORE SLEEP
meaning: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
bullets: Lie on the right side when possible, following Prophetic guidance.
Use the protection practices in this deck: Ayat al-Kursi and the three Quls.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari 6324; Prophetic sleep guidance.

title: PROTECTION: MORNING + EVENING
arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ، وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
translit: Bismi-llāhi lladhī lā yaḍurru maʿa-smihi shayʾun fi l-arḍi wa lā fi s-samāʾ, wa Huwa s-Samīʿu l-ʿAlīm.
meaning: In the name of Allah, with whose Name nothing in the earth or heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
bullets: Recite three times in the morning and three times in the evening.
source: Sunan Abi Dawud 5088; Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 3388.

title: SEEKING REFUGE FROM CREATED HARM
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
translit: Aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti llāhi t-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq.
meaning: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created.
source: Sahih Muslim 2708.

title: DUʿA FOR STEADFASTNESS
arabic: يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ، ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ
translit: Yā Muqalliba l-qulūb, thabbit qalbī ʿalā dīnik.
meaning: O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion.
source: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 2140.

title: SAJDAT AL-SHUKR
bullets: When a major blessing arrives or a calamity is lifted, prostrating in gratitude to Allah is permitted and recommended in Hanafi fiqh according to the relied-upon later position.
Perform one prostration with the conditions used for Sajdat al-Tilawah.
This is a prostration of gratitude, not a separate multi-rakʿah salah.
source: Hanafi fiqh on Sajdat al-Shukr; reported Prophetic practice of prostrating for glad tidings.
reflection: “If you are grateful, I will certainly give you more.”

title: RETURNING FROM A JOURNEY
bullets: When returning from travel, the Prophet ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam would begin by going to the masjid and praying two rakʿahs.
This is a Sunnah practice, not a condition of ending traveler status.
Traveler status itself ends according to the Hanafi residence rules when you re-enter your home locality.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim reports of praying two rakʿahs on return from travel.

title: JUMUʿAH: IF YOU ARRIVE LATE
bullets: If you arrive while the khutbah is underway, sit and listen; do not begin a voluntary prayer in Hanafi practice.
If you join the Jumuʿah prayer before the imam's final salam, Hanafi rulings treat you as having caught Jumuʿah and you complete the missed rakʿahs afterward.
If you miss Jumuʿah completely, pray Dhuhr instead.
source: Hanafi latecomer/Jumuʿah rulings; SeekersGuidance.
